pm_exper_user_4270_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I feel calmer and more confident when I have to speak in front of others?
pm_exper_user_4270_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Since you already feel more comfortable when playing drums, you could try thinking of your speech like a performance—practice it alone in your room first, maybe with some calming background instrumentals. Focus on the rhythm of your words and breathe deeply before starting. Imagine you’re just sharing music tips with a friend instead of speaking to the whole class.
(b) Since you enjoy hiking in nature, you could visualize yourself talking on a calm forest trail before stepping on stage. That mental scenery, along with slow, deep breaths, can help keep your mind from racing. Try to focus on the ‘adventure’ of telling your story like you would share a snapshot from your travels.
(c) Since many Indian families value academic achievement, you could think of your speech as just another subject to master through repetition. Practice it a few times with your family in the living room, then take a few deep breaths before the real thing. Treat it like answering a question in class with confidence.
(d) You could practice your speech a few times in front of a mirror or with a trusted friend, focusing on staying calm and breathing deeply before starting. Visualize delivering it successfully and keep your pace steady. Remember, the audience is usually rooting for you to do well.
